usage: Used to order a coffee in a café (ahwa) or restaurant. When ordering traditional Turkish-style coffee, Egyptians usually specify the sugar level immediately, such as 'mazboot' (medium sugar) or 'sada' (no sugar). The word 'ahwa' refers to both the drink itself and the traditional street-level coffee shops where it is served.

variants.label: Medium sugar (default)
variants.note: This is the default and most common way to order traditional Egyptian coffee.

variants.label: No sugar (black)
variants.note: Use this if you want your coffee completely without sugar.

variants.label: Extra sugar
variants.note: Used when you prefer your coffee very sweet.

variants.label: Female speaker ordering
variants.note: A common alternative for a woman ordering, instead of saying 'wa7ed ahwa'.

examples.arabic: لَوْ سَمَحْت، عَايِز اِتْنِين قَهْوَة مَظْبُوط.
examples.english: Excuse me, I want two medium-sugar coffees.

examples.transliteration: el ahwa di sokkarha zeyada awi.
examples.english: This coffee has way too much sugar.
Will you drink tea or coffee?
